# `nish/net/router`

A method and path router for HTTP servers, independent of the carrier: the same table answers an HTTP/1 request line and an HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 `:path`.

```ts
import {
  ROUTER_AMBIGUOUS,
  ROUTER_BAD_ESCAPE,
  ROUTER_BAD_METHOD,
  ROUTER_BAD_PATTERN,
  ROUTER_DUPLICATE,
  ROUTER_FULL,
  ROUTER_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED,
  ROUTER_NOT_FOUND,
  ROUTER_NO_ROOM,
  ROUTER_TOO_LONG,
  ROUTER_TOO_MANY_PARAMS,
  Router,
  RouterLimits,
  routerDecode,
} from "nish/net/router";
```

</scalar-card>

<scalar-callout type="info">

```text
const HOME: i32 = 0   // module constants, in the order the routes are added
const USER: i32 = 1
const router = new Router(new RouterLimits())
if (router.add("GET", "/") !== HOME || router.add("GET", "/users/:id") !== USER) panic(...)
// per request, with `params` made once beside the connection:
switch (router.match(p.head, p.methodStart, p.methodEnd, p.head, p.targetStart, p.targetEnd, params)) {
  case HOME: ... case USER: ... case ROUTER_NOT_FOUND: ...
}
```

</scalar-callout>

Nish has no function values, so a route is the index `add` answered, 0 for
the first and one more for each after, and the program dispatches on it
with `switch`, whose labels are module constants. A parameter is answered as a
`[start, end)` pair of offsets into the target, never as a copy, and
`routerDecode` percent-decodes one of them into a buffer the caller owns.

<scalar-detail title="The table is built once; a match allocates nothing">

`add` refuses a
duplicate, an ambiguous or an over-long pattern with a negative code and
adds nothing. `match` walks flat `i32` arrays the table grew and writes into
scratch the constructor sized, so a warmed server moves the arena by
nothing per request. A `Router` is therefore not reentrant: one match at a
time, which is what a connection loop does.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The rules">

**The rules** (`docs/wp43-http-app-layer.md` §2):

- The path is the target up to its first `?` (the query is left alone) and
  must start with `/`: the `*` of `OPTIONS *` and the authority form of
  `CONNECT` match nothing, so the program answers them before it routes.
- A path is split on `/` into segments; `/a/` has two, `a` and an empty one.
  A trailing slash is significant, and matching is on raw bytes, so `%2F`
  never splits a segment.
- A pattern segment is a literal, a parameter `:name` (one non-empty
  segment), or `*` as the last segment (the rest of the path, possibly
  empty, as one more pair). Precedence is literal, then parameter, then
  wildcard, segment by segment from the left; a branch that fails further
  down falls back to the next one. Every edge consumes one segment, so a
  lookup visits each node of the table at most once.
- A path that matches only routes of other methods answers
  `ROUTER_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, so a server can tell 405 from 404.

</scalar-detail>

Private helpers share the importing program's flat symbol namespace
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e), which is why each one carries the module's name.

## routerDecode

Percent-decodes `target[start .. end)`, one range `match` answered, into
`out` from 0, and answers the decoded length or a negative `ROUTER_*` code;
on a code nothing is written. `%2F` becomes `/` here, inside the one
parameter, because `match` split the path before anything was decoded. `+`
stays `+`: a space spelled `+` is the query's form encoding, not the path's.
The output may hold any byte, NUL and `/` included. Panics on a range
outside `target`.

```ts
function routerDecode(
  target: u8[],
  start: i32,
  end: i32,
  out: u8[],
): i32
```

## Router

A route table: a tree whose edges are path segments, kept in flat arrays.
Node 0 is the root, the point before the first segment; a node at depth `d`
has consumed `d` segments.

```ts
class Router
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Router(limits: RouterLimits)` | An empty table. Panics, naming the field, on a limit outside the range `RouterLimits` gives it. |
| `deepest: i32` | The most segments any route has: a path is split no further than one past it. |
| `endpointNext: i32[]` |  |
| `firstChild: i32[]` | Per node: its first literal child, or -1; siblings chain through `nextSibling`. |
| `firstEndpoint: i32[]` | Per node: the first route ending there, or -1; routes chain through `endpointNext`. |
| `found: i32[]` |  |
| `foundCount: i32` |  |
| `labelEnd: i32[]` |  |
| `labels: u8[]` | Every literal label, back to back. |
| `labelStart: i32[]` | Per node: its literal label, `labels[labelStart .. labelEnd)`; empty for a parameter or `*` node. |
| `maxMethods: i32` |  |
| `maxParams: i32` |  |
| `maxPatternBytes: i32` | The limits, copied out of the `RouterLimits` the table was made with. |
| `maxRoutes: i32` |  |
| `maxSegments: i32` |  |
| `methodBytes: u8[]` | The methods the table knows, `methodBytes[methodStart[m] .. methodEnd[m])`, compared exactly (RFC 9110 §9.1). |
| `methodEnd: i32[]` |  |
| `methodStart: i32[]` |  |
| `nextSibling: i32[]` | Per node: the next literal child of its parent, or -1. |
| `otherMethod: boolean` | During a match: whether a route of another method ended at the path's end. |
| `paramChild: i32[]` | Per node: its parameter child, or -1; one per node, since names take no part in matching. |
| `patEnd: i32[]` |  |
| `pathEnd: i32` |  |
| `patKind: i32[]` | `add`'s scratch: each pattern segment's kind and span in the pattern. |
| `patStart: i32[]` |  |
| `routeMethod: i32[]` | Per route: its method's index into `methodStart`, the next route ending at its node, and its parameter pairs. |
| `routeParams: i32[]` |  |
| `segEnd: i32[]` |  |
| `segments: i32` | During a match: how many segments the path has, where it ends, the method's index, and the pairs in `found`. |
| `segStart: i32[]` | `match`'s scratch, sized by the constructor: each segment's span, then the pairs found so far. |
| `visited: i32` | The nodes the last `match` visited: never more than `nodeCount()`, which the tests pin. |
| `wanted: i32` |  |
| `wildChild: i32[]` | Per node: its `*` child, or -1. |
| `add(method: string, pattern: string): i32` | Adds the route `method pattern` and answers its index, counting from 0, or a negative `ROUTER_*` code; a refused pattern adds nothing. Whether a pattern is refused never depends on the order routes were added in. |
| `addChild(node: i32, pattern: string, k: i32): i32` | Adds the child of `node` that pattern segment `k` leads to, and answers it. |
| `childFor(node: i32, pattern: string, k: i32): i32` | The child of `node` that pattern segment `k` leads to, or -1. |
| `endpointFor(node: i32): i32` | The route of the wanted method ending at `node`, or -1, noting a route of another method there. |
| `lastVisited(): i32` | How many nodes the last `match` visited. |
| `match(method: u8[], mStart: i32, mEnd: i32, target: u8[], tStart: i32, tEnd: i32, params: i32[]): i32` | The route `method[mStart .. mEnd)` and `target[tStart .. tEnd)` reach, or a negative `ROUTER_*` code. On a route, its parameters are written to `params` as `[start, end)` offsets into `target`, two slots each, in the pattern's order, and a final `*` as one more pair; on a refusal `params` is untouched. Panics on a range outside its array. |
| `methodIndex(method: string): i32` | The index of `method` among the methods the table knows, or -1. |
| `nodeCount(): i32` | How many nodes the tree has, the root included: the most one `match` visits. |
| `paramCount(route: i32): i32` | How many `[start, end)` pairs `route` answers: its parameters, and one more for a final `*`. |
| `routes(): i32` | How many routes the table holds; the next `add` answers this index. |
| `splitPattern(pattern: string): i32` | Splits `pattern`, which starts with `/`, into `patKind`/`patStart`/`patEnd` and answers how many segments it has, or the code that refuses it. |
| `walk(target: u8[], node: i32, depth: i32): i32` | The route below `node`, which has consumed `depth` segments, for the wanted method, or -1. Literal, then parameter, then `*`: the first branch that reaches a route wins, and a branch that does not is left with the pairs it pushed popped. |

## RouterLimits

What a `Router` holds and refuses past. Each field has a default a server
can use as it is; the constructor panics on a value no table could work with.

```ts
class RouterLimits
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new RouterLimits()` |  |
| `maxMethods: i32` | The most distinct methods (1 to 64). |
| `maxParams: i32` | The most parameters in one pattern, a final `*` counted (0 to 256). |
| `maxPatternBytes: i32` | The longest pattern, in bytes (1 to 65536). |
| `maxRoutes: i32` | The most routes in the table (1 to 1048576). |
| `maxSegments: i32` | The most segments in one pattern (1 to 256): the deepest a route can be. |

<scalar-card title="-4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`ROUTER_AMBIGUOUS: i32`

`add`: a `*` that is not the last segment, where how much it takes would be a guess.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-10" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`ROUTER_BAD_ESCAPE: i32`

`routerDecode`: a `%` not followed by two hex digits.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`ROUTER_BAD_METHOD: i32`

`add`: the method is not a token of 1 to 32 bytes.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`ROUTER_BAD_PATTERN: i32`

`add`: the pattern is empty, does not start with `/`, or misuses `:`, `*`, `%`, `?` or a byte outside `!` to `~`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`ROUTER_DUPLICATE: i32`

`add`: the method already has a route of this shape, whatever its parameters are called.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`ROUTER_FULL: i32`

`add`: the table holds `RouterLimits.maxRoutes` routes or `maxMethods` methods already.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`ROUTER_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED: i32`

`match`: the path matches only routes of other methods.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`ROUTER_NOT_FOUND: i32`

`match`: no route's pattern matches the path, or the target is not `/`-rooted.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-11" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`ROUTER_NO_ROOM: i32`

`routerDecode`: the decoded bytes do not fit `out`; nothing was written.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`ROUTER_TOO_LONG: i32`

`add`: the pattern is over `RouterLimits`' bytes, segments or parameters.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-9" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`ROUTER_TOO_MANY_PARAMS: i32`

`match`: the route matched, but its parameters need more than `params` holds; nothing was written.

</scalar-card>
